_README: Pins a specific opponent to a specific level's stage, overriding the
normal pick.
WRITTEN BY HAND, like rules.json and booster_standing.json.
export_data.py never overwrites it — Cameron edits this file directly.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The workbook's Levels tab has no column that says who
you fight at each stage of a level. By default the game works this out
itself: every opponent whose Opponents-tab 'stages' list names that STxx
is eligible, and the game picks one of them (see BattleSetup.gd,
_opponent_for()). That default is DYNAMIC on purpose — add an opponent to
the workbook and eligible-for-that-stage levels pick them up with no
level data to edit. Cameron confirmed this 2026-09-22.
Sometimes a level needs a NAMED opponent regardless of who else is
eligible — the caucus rival in a party caucus should be the same MP every
time, say. That is what this file is for: one entry per level+stage slot
you want pinned. A level with no entry here just uses the dynamic pick.
Most levels will have none.
HOW TO USE IT. Add one object per pin to the 'overrides' list:
level_id   the level, e.g. "LV03"
slot       which Stage ID column on that level's row, 1-10, matching
stage_1 .. stage_10 on the Levels tab
opp_id     the opponent to use, from opponents.json — must be one whose
own 'stages' list already includes the STxx in that slot,
or the game logs a warning and falls back to the dynamic
pick rather than seating someone in a room they are not
written to be eligible for
COMMITTEE STAGES (ST01, ST09-ST18) read this file too, but differently:
a committee has a whole roster, not one opponent, so an override there
means 'make sure this person is on the roster and is its chair' rather
than 'replace the roster'. The chair is still picked the same way
otherwise — see BattleSetup.gd's [DEFAULT] note on chair selection.
Nothing is in here yet. Every level currently uses the dynamic pick.
